symbols.name: first vector space
symbols.meaning: The first of the two vector spaces being tensored.
symbols.quote: Let $E$ and $F$ be vector spaces over $\mathbb{C}$.

symbols.name: second vector space
symbols.meaning: The second of the two vector spaces being tensored.
symbols.quote: Let $E$ and $F$ be vector spaces over $\mathbb{C}$.

symbols.name: general vector of E
symbols.meaning: A general vector of the space E.
symbols.quote: Every $e\in E$ is a general vector of $E$, and every $f\in F$ a general vector of $F$.

symbols.name: general vector of F
symbols.meaning: A general vector of the space F.
symbols.quote: Every $e\in E$ is a general vector of $E$, and every $f\in F$ a general vector of $F$.

symbols.name: basis vector of E
symbols.meaning: The i-th vector of a fixed basis of E.
symbols.quote: Let $e_1,\dots,e_p$ be a basis of $E$ and $f_1,\dots,f_q$ a basis of $F$, where $e_i$ is the $i$th basis vector of $E$, $f_j$ the $j$th of $F$, $p$ and $q$ are the numbers of basis vectors, and $1\le i\le p$, $1\le j\le q$.

symbols.name: basis vector of F
symbols.meaning: The j-th vector of a fixed basis of F.
symbols.quote: Let $e_1,\dots,e_p$ be a basis of $E$ and $f_1,\dots,f_q$ a basis of $F$, where $e_i$ is the $i$th basis vector of $E$, $f_j$ the $j$th of $F$, $p$ and $q$ are the numbers of basis vectors, and $1\le i\le p$, $1\le j\le q$.

symbols.name: basis size of E
symbols.meaning: The number of basis vectors of E, which counts the vectors e_1 through e_p.
symbols.quote: Let $e_1,\dots,e_p$ be a basis of $E$ and $f_1,\dots,f_q$ a basis of $F$, where $e_i$ is the $i$th basis vector of $E$, $f_j$ the $j$th of $F$, $p$ and $q$ are the numbers of basis vectors, and $1\le i\le p$, $1\le j\le q$.

symbols.name: basis size of F
symbols.meaning: The number of basis vectors of F, which counts the vectors f_1 through f_q.
symbols.quote: Let $e_1,\dots,e_p$ be a basis of $E$ and $f_1,\dots,f_q$ a basis of $F$, where $e_i$ is the $i$th basis vector of $E$, $f_j$ the $j$th of $F$, $p$ and $q$ are the numbers of basis vectors, and $1\le i\le p$, $1\le j\le q$.

symbols.name: basis index of E
symbols.meaning: An index of the basis vectors e_i of E, running from 1 to p.
symbols.quote: Let $e_1,\dots,e_p$ be a basis of $E$ and $f_1,\dots,f_q$ a basis of $F$, where $e_i$ is the $i$th basis vector of $E$, $f_j$ the $j$th of $F$, $p$ and $q$ are the numbers of basis vectors, and $1\le i\le p$, $1\le j\le q$.

symbols.name: basis index of F
symbols.meaning: An index of the basis vectors f_j of F, running from 1 to q.
symbols.quote: Let $e_1,\dots,e_p$ be a basis of $E$ and $f_1,\dots,f_q$ a basis of $F$, where $e_i$ is the $i$th basis vector of $E$, $f_j$ the $j$th of $F$, $p$ and $q$ are the numbers of basis vectors, and $1\le i\le p$, $1\le j\le q$.

symbols.name: linear map on E
symbols.meaning: A linear map of the space E, one factor of the tensor product of maps.
symbols.quote: Let $A$ be a linear map of $E$ and $T$ of $F$.

symbols.name: linear map on F
symbols.meaning: A linear map of the space F, the second factor of the tensor product of maps.
symbols.quote: Let $A$ be a linear map of $E$ and $T$ of $F$.

symbols.name: selected bit count
symbols.meaning: The number of selected bits on which the butterfly acts, one factor per bit.
symbols.quote: Here $D$ counts the selected bits, not the address field $D$.

relations.quote: The tensor product of one-dimensional transforms is built from one [Discrete Fourier transform](fourier-transform.md) per axis.
